en: middle part of a mountain; halfway up

examples.ko: 산 중턱에 작은 절이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small temple halfway up the mountain.
The fog came down to the middle of the mountain.

examples.ko: 중턱쯤 올라가면 물을 마실 수 있는 곳이 나와요.
examples.en: If you climb about halfway, you will find a place to drink water.

examples.ko: 힘들어서 정상까지 못 가고 중턱에서 내려왔어요.
examples.en: It was hard, so I could not reach the top and came down from halfway.

examples.ko: 언덕 중턱에 있는 집이라서 경치가 좋아요.
examples.en: The house is on the side of a hill, so the view is nice.

examples.ko: 저기 중턱에 있는 벤치에서 잠깐 쉴까요?
examples.en: Shall we rest for a moment on the bench halfway up there?

explain: 산이나 언덕의 꼭대기와 아래 사이를 말할 때 써요. '산 중턱'처럼 산과 같이 쓰는 경우가 대부분이에요. 건물이나 책의 가운데에는 쓰지 않고 '중간'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it for the stretch between the top and the bottom of a mountain or hill, almost always as '산 중턱'. For the middle of a building or a book, say '중간' instead.

examples.en: I put egg strips on top of the spicy noodles.

examples.ko: 어머니가 노른자와 흰자를 따로 지단으로 부치셨어요.
examples.en: My mother fried the yolk and the white separately into thin egg sheets.
Egg garnish looks nice when it is cut thin.
Kimbap is softer when you add egg strips.
Banquet noodles usually come with egg strips on top.
Please teach me how to make egg garnish.

explain: 국수, 떡국, 잡채, 김밥에 올리거나 넣어서 색을 내는 데 많이 써요. 노른자로 만들면 노란색, 흰자로 만들면 흰색 지단이 돼요. 계란말이나 계란프라이와는 다른 음식이에요.
explain_en: It adds color to noodles, rice cake soup, japchae, and kimbap. Yolk makes yellow strips and egg white makes white ones. It is a different dish from '계란말이' or '계란프라이'.

examples.en: The corner of this paper is a right angle.
The two lines meet at a right angle.
I placed the desk at a right angle to the wall.
I drew a right angle with a set square.

examples.ko: 길이 갑자기 직각으로 꺾여서 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: The road turned sharply at a right angle, and I got lost.
Find the area of the right triangle.

explain: 90도가 직각이고, 90도보다 작으면 예각, 크면 둔각이에요. 길이나 선이 딱 꺾일 때도 '직각으로 꺾이다'라고 해요. 보통 '직각으로' 또는 '직각 삼각형'처럼 붙여서 써요.
explain_en: 90 degrees is a right angle, smaller is '예각', and larger is '둔각'. A road or line that bends sharply can also '직각으로 꺾이다'. It usually appears as '직각으로' or '직각 삼각형'.

examples.en: A march was playing at the graduation ceremony.
A march has a steady beat, so it is good for walking.
The children walked in time with the march.
The band played a lively march.
They always play marches at the sports day.

examples.ko: 행진곡 같은 노래를 들으면 힘이 나요.
examples.en: Listening to a song like a march gives me energy.

explain: '결혼행진곡', '군대 행진곡'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여서 많이 써요. 박자가 일정해서 발을 맞춰 걷기 좋은 음악이에요. 걷는 행동은 '행진'이고, 뒤에 '곡'이 붙으면 음악이 돼요.
explain_en: It often comes with a word in front, like '결혼행진곡' or '군대 행진곡'. The beat is steady, so people can walk in step. '행진' is the walking itself; adding '곡' makes it a piece of music.

examples.en: I started eating brown rice for my health.
Brown rice is a little harder than white rice.

examples.ko: 저는 현미랑 콩을 섞어서 밥을 지어요.
examples.en: I mix brown rice and beans when I cook rice.
I bought a bag of brown rice at the supermarket.
Brown rice tea tastes nutty.
Snacks made with brown rice taste plain and clean.

explain: 흰쌀(백미)과 비교해서 자주 말해요. 건강식이나 다이어트 이야기에 많이 나와요. '현미밥', '현미차', '현미 과자'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: People often compare it with white rice (백미). It comes up in talk about healthy eating and diets. It is used before other words, as in '현미밥', '현미차', and '현미 과자'.

examples.en: The violin and cello are string instruments.
I took a string instrument part in the school orchestra.
String instruments sound soft.
Among string instruments, I like the cello best.
The gayageum is a typical Korean string instrument.
This piece is played with only string instruments.

explain: 줄이 있는 악기를 모두 부르는 말이에요. 부는 악기는 '관악기', 치는 악기는 '타악기'로 짝을 이뤄 외우면 좋아요. 악기마다 동사가 달라서 바이올린은 '켜다', 가야금은 '타다', 기타는 '치다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '관악기' (wind) and '타악기' (percussion). Each instrument takes its own verb: '켜다' for the violin, '타다' for the gayageum, and '치다' for the guitar.

examples.en: He did the job he was given admirably.
The child passed the hard exam with flying colors.
I am proud of my son, who grew up so well.
The players finished the tough game admirably.

examples.ko: 새 직원이 팀에서 맡은 역할을 훌륭히 소화했어요.
examples.en: The new employee handled their role on the team very well.
Everyone prepared so well that the presentation went great.

explain: 뜻이 같은 '훌륭하게'가 말할 때는 더 흔해요. '훌륭히'는 글이나 격식 있는 자리에서 칭찬할 때 잘 어울려요. 뒤에 '해내다', '자라다', '마치다'처럼 결과를 말하는 동사가 자주 와요.
explain_en: '훌륭하게' is more common in speech. '훌륭히' fits writing and formal praise. It is often followed by result verbs like '해내다', '자라다', and '마치다'.

examples.en: We play rock, paper, scissors to bet on lunch.
I lost at rock, paper, scissors, so I will go first.
The kids are playing rock, paper, scissors.

examples.ko: 가위바위보 해서 이긴 사람이 먼저 골라요!
examples.en: The winner of rock, paper, scissors picks first!

examples.ko: 가위바위보를 세 번 했는데 계속 비겼어요.
examples.en: We played rock, paper, scissors three times and kept tying.
Shall we do rock, paper, scissors to decide who goes first?

explain: 순서나 당번을 빨리 정할 때 한국 사람들이 자주 해요. 동사는 '하다'를 써서 '가위바위보를 하다'라고 해요. 이기면 '이기다', 지면 '지다', 같으면 '비기다'라고 하고, 시작할 때는 다 같이 '가위바위보!' 하고 외쳐요.
explain_en: Koreans use it all the time to settle turns or chores quickly. The verb is '하다': '가위바위보를 하다'. Then '이기다' (win), '지다' (lose), '비기다' (tie). Players shout '가위바위보!' together to start.

examples.ko: 친구 모임에서 신입생이 개인기를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: At the gathering, the freshman showed off a party trick.
My younger brother's special talent is doing impressions.
This player's individual skill is outstanding.

examples.ko: 개인기를 보여 달라고 해서 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: They asked for a party trick, so I sang a song.
In team games, teamwork matters more than individual skill.
I had no party trick, so I just laughed.

explain: 쓰임이 두 가지예요. 축구나 농구에서는 드리블 같은 선수 한 사람의 기술이고, 모임에서는 성대모사나 춤처럼 보여 주는 재주예요. '개인기를 보여 주다', '개인기가 좋다'처럼 써요. 팀워크와 반대로 말할 때도 나와요.
explain_en: It has two uses. In sports like soccer or basketball it means one player's skill, such as dribbling. At a gathering it means a trick, like an impression or a dance. It is also set against teamwork.

examples.en: There is a checkpoint at the highway entrance.
The police stopped the car at the checkpoint.

examples.ko: 검문소를 지날 때 신분증을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I showed my ID when passing the checkpoint.
There are many checkpoints near the border.

examples.ko: 검문소 앞에서 차가 길게 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: Cars lined up long in front of the checkpoint.

examples.ko: 검문소의 군인이 가방을 열어 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: The soldier at the checkpoint told me to open my bag.

explain: 공항 보안 검색대나 입국 심사와는 달라요. 검문소는 도로나 국경 근처에서 차를 세우고 사람을 확인하는 곳이에요. '검문을 받다', '검문에 걸리다'처럼 '검문'과 같이 외워 두세요.
explain_en: It differs from an airport security line or immigration. A '검문소' stops vehicles and checks people on roads or near borders. Learn it with '검문', as in '검문을 받다' and '검문에 걸리다'.

examples.ko: 이 일은 경험자만 지원할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only experienced people can apply for this job.
Hearing from someone with experience helped me.
I feel at ease when an experienced person is beside me.
Our shop hires experienced people first.

examples.ko: 그는 이 분야의 경험자라서 설명을 잘해요.
examples.en: He is experienced in this field, so he explains well.
An experienced person and a beginner were put in the same group.

explain: 구인 공고의 '경험자 우대'라는 말로 많이 봐요. 반대말은 '초보자'나 '미경험자'예요. 일 이야기에서는 '경력자'를 더 자주 써요. '경험자'는 일뿐 아니라 여행, 시험 같은 일상 경험에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: You often see '경험자 우대' in job ads. Its opposites are '초보자' and '미경험자'. For work, '경력자' is more common. '경험자' also works for everyday experiences like travel or exams.

en: crossing the finish line; scoring a goal

examples.en: The marathon runner crossed the finish line first.
My family is waiting at the finish line.
The shot went in and it was a goal.

examples.ko: 마지막 주자가 골인하는 순간 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Everyone clapped the moment the last runner crossed the line.

examples.ko: 둘은 오랜 연애 끝에 결혼에 골인할 거예요.
examples.en: After a long courtship, the two will finally get married.
I handed water to the runner who had finished.

explain: 달리기에서는 결승선에 들어오는 것, 축구나 농구에서는 공이 골대에 들어가는 것에 써요. 축구 점수를 말할 때는 그냥 '골'을 더 많이 써요. 영어의 goal처럼 '목표'라는 뜻으로는 쓰지 않아요. 그럴 때는 '목표'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 둘은 삼 년 연애 끝에 결혼에 골인했어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연애를 오래 한 두 사람이 마침내 결혼하게 될 때 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light, friendly way to say a couple finally got married after dating for a while.

explain_en: It means reaching the finish line in a race, or the ball going into the net in soccer or basketball. For a soccer score, people usually just say '골'. It does not mean 'goal' as in an aim; for that, use '목표'.

examples.ko: 구제역 때문에 소를 키우는 농가가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Farms that raise cattle are struggling because of foot-and-mouth disease.
The news says foot-and-mouth disease has spread.
When it breaks out, they block entry to farms.
The government supports vaccination against foot-and-mouth disease.

examples.ko: 지난겨울에 구제역이 돌아서 고기 값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Foot-and-mouth disease went around last winter, so meat prices rose.
The village where it was found stayed quiet for a while.

explain: 소, 돼지 같은 동물이 걸리는 병이라서 사람의 병에는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스에서는 '구제역이 발생하다', '구제역이 확산되다', '구제역 방역'처럼 써요. 새가 걸리는 병은 '조류인플루엔자'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: It is a disease of animals such as cattle and pigs, never of people. In the news: '구제역이 발생하다', '구제역이 확산되다', and '구제역 방역'. A disease in birds is '조류인플루엔자', a different term.

examples.en: My mother likes precious metals like gold rings.
I ordered wedding rings at a jewelry shop.

examples.ko: 귀금속은 값이 비싸서 잘 보관해야 해요.
examples.en: Precious metals are expensive, so they must be stored well.
A thief stole jewelry from the house.
Gold and silver are typical precious metals.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 귀금속을 많이 가져가지 않아요.
examples.en: I do not bring much jewelry when I travel.

explain: 금, 은, 백금처럼 값이 많이 나가는 금속과 그것으로 만든 장신구를 같이 부를 때 써요. 값싼 '액세서리'와는 느낌이 달라요. 가게 간판에는 '귀금속'이나 '금은방'이 많이 붙어 있어요.
explain_en: It covers valuable metals like gold, silver, and platinum, plus jewelry made from them. It feels different from cheap '액세서리'. Shop signs often say '귀금속' or '금은방'.

examples.en: In spring we make soybean paste soup with shepherd's purse.
Grandmother dug up shepherd's purse in the field and brought it.

examples.ko: 냉이는 향이 강해서 처음엔 낯설 수 있어요.
examples.en: Its scent is strong, so it may feel unfamiliar at first.
Shepherd's purse is already out at the market.
I blanched the greens and mixed them with red pepper paste.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 냉이랑 달래 생각이 나요.
examples.en: When spring comes, I think of shepherd's purse and wild chives.

explain: 봄을 알리는 나물이라서 3월 즈음 시장에 많이 나와요. 된장국이나 무침으로 먹고, 뿌리까지 같이 먹는 게 특징이에요. 비슷한 봄나물로 '달래'와 '쑥'이 있어요. '냉이를 캐다', '냉이를 무치다'처럼 동사와 같이 외워요.
explain_en: It is a spring herald, widely sold around March. People eat it in soybean paste soup or as a seasoned side dish, roots included. Other spring greens are '달래' and '쑥'. Learn it with '냉이를 캐다' and '냉이를 무치다'.

examples.en: I was a bridesmaid at my friend's wedding.
My younger sister became my older sister's bridesmaid.
We picked the bridesmaid dresses together.

examples.ko: 신부 들러리들이 꽃을 들고 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The bride's attendants stood holding flowers.

examples.ko: 들러리는 보통 신부와 친한 친구가 맡아요.
examples.en: A bridesmaid is usually a close friend of the bride.
I gave a thank-you gift to the bridesmaid.

explain: 결혼식에서 신부나 신랑 곁에 서는 사람을 말하고, 동사는 '서다'를 써서 '들러리를 서다'라고 해요. 누구의 들러리인지 앞에 붙여서 '신부 들러리'처럼 써요. 비유로도 많이 써서 아래 표현을 같이 보세요.

phrases.example: 이번 대회는 우승자가 정해져 있어서 저는 들러리만 선 것 같아요.
phrases.en: just be there to make someone else look good
phrases.nuance_ko: 중심이 아니라 다른 사람을 돋보이게 해 주는 역할만 한다는 비유예요. 조금 서운한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for playing only a supporting role while someone else is the star. It carries a slightly resentful feeling.

explain_en: It refers to someone standing beside the bride or groom at a wedding, with the verb '서다': '들러리를 서다'. Put the person in front, as in '신부 들러리'. It is also used figuratively; see the expression below.

en: lift out; carry out; take out

examples.en: To move out, I lifted the big desk out of the room.
Please carry the sofa out of the living room.
I will move the fridge out to clean.

examples.ko: 낡은 문짝을 들어내고 새 문을 달았어요.
examples.en: We took off the old door and put up a new one.
Two people have to carry out the heavy load.

examples.ko: 방을 넓게 쓰려고 침대를 들어내는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people remove the bed to use the room more widely.

explain: 안에 있는 큰 물건을 들어서 밖으로 옮길 때 써요. '꺼내다'는 작은 물건에도 쓰지만, '들어내다'는 무거워서 번쩍 들어야 하는 물건에 어울려요. 발음이 같은 '드러내다'(숨은 것을 보이다)와는 글자가 달라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심해요.
explain_en: Use it when you lift a big item and move it out. '꺼내다' works for small things too, but '들어내다' suits heavy things you must hoist. It sounds the same as '드러내다' (to reveal), so watch the spelling.

examples.en: In spring, cherry blossoms are in full bloom in the park.
Roses were in full bloom in the garden.

examples.ko: 꽃이 만발한 길을 걸으면 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: Walking down a road full of blooming flowers feels good.

examples.ko: 산에 진달래가 만발할 때 등산을 가요.
examples.en: I go hiking when azaleas are in full bloom on the mountain.

examples.ko: 유채꽃이 만발하는 제주도에 가 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to visit Jeju, where rape blossoms bloom everywhere.
The cosmos were in full bloom, so I took many photos.

explain: '피다'는 꽃 한 송이에도 쓰지만, '만발하다'는 꽃이 가득 핀 풍경에 써요. 주로 글이나 방송에서 쓰는 느낌이고, '꽃이 만발하다'처럼 꽃 이름과 같이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '활짝 피었어요'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '피다' can describe a single flower, but '만발하다' describes a scene full of blossoms. It sounds more like writing or broadcasts, and pairs with flowers: '꽃이 만발하다'. In daily talk, people say '활짝 피었어요'.

examples.ko: 인터넷이 안 돼서 모뎀을 껐다 켰어요.
examples.en: The internet was down, so I turned the modem off and on.
A modem and a router are different devices.

examples.ko: 이 모뎀은 십 년 전에 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought this modem ten years ago.
The lights on the modem do not turn on.

examples.ko: 통신사 기사님이 와서 모뎀을 바꿔 주셨어요.
examples.en: A technician from the carrier came and replaced the modem.
In the old days, modems made a loud noise.

explain: 인터넷이 안 될 때 '모뎀을 껐다 켜 보세요'라는 말을 많이 들어요. 와이파이를 퍼뜨리는 '공유기'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 모뎀은 인터넷 회선과 연결하는 기계예요. 요즘은 둘이 한 기계로 합쳐진 것도 있어요.
explain_en: When the internet fails, you often hear '모뎀을 껐다 켜 보세요'. People mix it up with a '공유기' (router that spreads Wi-Fi), but the modem connects to the internet line. Some devices now combine both.

examples.en: After sitting for a long time, my leg went numb.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 남의 아픔에 너무 무감각해요.
examples.en: That person is too insensitive to others' pain.
It was so cold that my fingertips went numb.
He keeps looking out the window with a blank expression.

examples.ko: 나쁜 소식에 자꾸 무감각해지는 게 무서워요.
examples.en: I am scared that I keep becoming numb to bad news.
If the numbness lasts long, go to a hospital.

explain: 몸에서는 느낌이 없는 상태에, 마음에서는 남의 일에 아무 느낌이 없는 상태에 써요. '무관심'은 관심을 두지 않는 태도이고, '무감각'은 느끼는 힘이 둔한 상태예요. 보통 '무감각하다', '무감각해지다'로 써요.
explain_en: For the body it means no feeling; for the mind it means feeling nothing about others' matters. '무관심' is an attitude of not caring, while '무감각' is a dulled ability to feel. Usually used as '무감각하다' or '무감각해지다'.

examples.en: I am jobless now, so I am looking for work.
I wrote 'unemployed' in the occupation box on the form.
I get anxious when the jobless period gets long.
I was jobless but got a job last month.

examples.ko: 무직인 사람도 지원금을 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even people without jobs can apply for the support money.
My jobless older brother helps with the housework.

explain: 서류의 직업 칸이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때는 '백수'라고 해요. 학생이나 주부는 보통 '무직' 대신 '학생', '주부'라고 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word seen in the occupation box on forms and in the news. Friends casually say '백수'. Students and homemakers usually write '학생' or '주부' instead of '무직'.

examples.en: I overslept and rushed to school.
I hurriedly cleaned when I heard guests were coming.
After getting the call, I rushed to the hospital.
I hastily wrote the report the day before the deadline.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 사람들이 부랴부랴 빨래를 걷었어요.
examples.en: When it rained, people hurried to take in the laundry.
I left in such a rush that I forgot my wallet.

explain: 시간이 없어서 서두르는 모습인데, 미리 준비하지 못해서 급하게 한다는 느낌이 들어요. '빨리'는 속도만 말하고 '부랴부랴'는 당황한 느낌이 같이 있어요. 늘 '부랴부랴 + 동사'로 쓰고 형용사 앞에는 안 써요.
explain_en: It describes rushing because time is short, with a feeling of not being prepared. '빨리' only says fast; '부랴부랴' adds a flustered feel. It always goes before a verb, never before an adjective.

examples.en: I play the viola in the orchestra.
The viola is a bit bigger than the violin.

examples.ko: 동생은 비올라 수업을 받은 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has taken viola lessons for a year.
The viola sounds lower and warmer than the violin.
We are short one viola player.
In this piece, the viola carries the melody.

explain: 바이올린보다 크고 첼로보다 작아서 소리 높이도 그 사이예요. 연주할 때는 '연주하다'가 가장 무난하고, 바이올린처럼 '켜다'도 쓸 수 있어요. 오케스트라 이야기에서 바이올린, 첼로와 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is bigger than the violin and smaller than the cello, so its pitch sits between them. '연주하다' is the safest verb, and '켜다' works as with the violin. It often appears with the violin and cello in orchestra talk.

examples.en: The dove is a symbol of peace.
This city's emblem is a tall tower.
We chose the tiger as the school's emblem.

examples.ko: 상징물을 보면 그 나라의 문화를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can learn a country's culture from its symbols.
The rose of Sharon is one of our country's symbols.
We are making a new company emblem.

explain: 나라, 도시, 학교, 회사처럼 어떤 단체를 대표하는 물건이나 동물에 써요. '상징'은 평화, 사랑 같은 생각에도 쓰지만 '상징물'은 눈에 보이는 것에만 써요. '마스코트'는 캐릭터 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used for an object or animal that represents a country, city, school, or company. '상징' also covers ideas like peace or love, but '상징물' covers only visible things. '마스코트' feels more like a character.

examples.en: I put on lotion after washing up.
I packed my toiletries and went on a trip.
There are two washbasins in the bathroom.
In the morning I wash up and brush my teeth.
The hotel has toiletries prepared.

examples.ko: 세면할 때 물을 오래 틀어 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not leave the water running long when washing up.

explain: 혼자서는 잘 안 쓰고 '세면대', '세면도구' 같은 말에서 많이 봐요. 일상에서는 '세면했어요'보다 '세수했어요'라고 말해요. '세면'은 안내문이나 설명서에 나오는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It rarely stands alone and appears in words like '세면대' and '세면도구'. In daily speech people say '세수했어요' rather than '세면했어요'. '세면' is a slightly formal word found in notices and manuals.

examples.en: The tax rate went up a little this year.
Tax rates differ by country.

examples.ko: 세율이 낮은 나라로 회사를 옮기는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: Some companies move to countries with low tax rates.
A high tax rate applies to this item.
The government announced it will lower the tax rate.

examples.ko: 세율을 알아야 정확한 세금을 계산할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need to know the rate to calculate the exact tax.

explain: '세금'은 내는 돈이고 '세율'은 그 돈을 정하는 비율이에요. '소득세율', '부가가치세율'처럼 앞에 세금 이름을 붙여요. '세율이 오르다/내리다'와 '세율을 올리다/내리다'를 짝으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: '세금' is the money you pay and '세율' is the rate that decides it. Put the tax name in front, as in '소득세율'. Learn '세율이 오르다/내리다' together with '세율을 올리다/내리다'.

examples.en: The computer lab is on the third floor.
After class I practiced in the practice room.

examples.ko: 실습실이 밤 열 시까지 열려 있어요.
examples.en: The practice room is open until ten at night.
You have to wear gloves in the chemistry lab.
A new practice room opened, and students like it.
You must apply in advance to use the practice room.

explain: '교실'은 앉아서 듣는 수업을 하는 곳이고 '실습실'은 직접 손으로 해 보는 수업을 하는 곳이에요. '컴퓨터 실습실', '요리 실습실'처럼 앞에 과목을 붙여요. 과학 실험을 하는 방은 '실험실'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A '교실' is for sitting and listening; a '실습실' is for hands-on classes. Put the subject in front: '컴퓨터 실습실', '요리 실습실'. A room for science experiments is a '실험실'.

examples.en: I stuck a magnet on the side of the fridge.
I wrote my name on the side of the book.
There is a big painting on the side of the building.

examples.ko: 우유갑 옆면을 보면 날짜가 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: If you look at the side of the milk carton, a date is printed.
The side of the car got scratched.

examples.ko: 택배 상자 옆면에 주소가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The address is stuck on the side of the parcel box.

explain: 앞면, 뒷면과 짝을 이루는 말이고 물건의 좌우 쪽 면을 가리켜요. 사람의 얼굴에는 '옆면'보다 '옆모습'을 더 자주 써요. 설명서나 안내문에서 위치를 정확히 말할 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It pairs with '앞면' and '뒷면' and points to the left or right surface of an object. For a person's face, '옆모습' is more common. It often appears in manuals and notices that give exact positions.

examples.en: This steak is full of juices.

examples.ko: 육즙을 살리려면 센 불에서 먼저 구워요.
examples.en: To keep the juices in, sear it first over high heat.
When I bit into the dumpling, juice flowed out.
I ate a juicy hamburger.

examples.ko: 고기를 잠깐 두어야 육즙이 안에 남아요.
examples.en: Let the meat rest a bit so the juices stay inside.
Juicy meat gets softer the more you chew.

explain: 고기에서 나오는 국물이고, 맛있다는 칭찬에 자주 나와요. '육즙이 풍부하다', '육즙이 흐르다'처럼 써요. 과일은 '과즙'이라고 하고, 고기나 뼈를 끓여 낸 국물은 '육수'라서 달라요.
explain_en: It is the juice that comes out of meat and often shows up in praise: '육즙이 풍부하다', '육즙이 흐르다'. Fruit juice is '과즙', and broth boiled from meat or bones is '육수', a different word.

examples.en: My father subscribes to an architecture trade magazine.
This article was published in a medical journal.

examples.ko: 전문지에는 일반 잡지보다 어려운 말이 많아요.
examples.en: Specialist magazines have more difficult words than general ones.

examples.ko: 전문지 기자로 일한 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since I started as a trade magazine reporter.

examples.ko: 그 분야 전문지를 읽으면 최신 소식을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: Reading that field's trade magazine tells you the latest news.

examples.ko: 전문지에 글을 실으려면 심사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To publish in a specialist magazine, you must pass a review.

explain: 앞에 분야 이름을 붙여서 '의학 전문지', '컴퓨터 전문지'라고 해요. 여러 분야를 다루는 신문은 '종합지'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 그 일을 하는 사람이 많이 읽어서 말이 조금 어려워요.
explain_en: Put the field before it: '의학 전문지', '컴퓨터 전문지'. Its counterpart is '종합지', which covers many fields. Readers are mostly people in that line of work, so the language is a little harder.

examples.en: My mother was a full-time homemaker for a long time.
I became a full-time homemaker after my child was born.
Being a full-time homemaker does not mean resting.

examples.ko: 이웃집 아주머니는 전업주부라서 낮에 집에 계세요.
examples.en: The neighbor lady is a full-time homemaker, so she is home in the daytime.

examples.ko: 전업주부의 일을 월급으로 따지면 금액이 꽤 커요.
examples.en: If you count a homemaker's work as a salary, the amount is quite large.
I quit being a full-time homemaker and started working.

explain: '주부'만 써도 되지만 '전업주부'는 밖에서 일하지 않고 집안일을 한다는 점을 분명히 해요. 일하면서 살림도 하는 사람은 '맞벌이 주부'나 '워킹맘'이라고 해요. 요즘은 남자에게도 '전업주부'라고 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: '주부' alone is fine, but '전업주부' makes clear that the person does not work outside the home. Someone who works and also runs the home is a '맞벌이 주부' or '워킹맘'. These days it can also describe men.

examples.en: The shop owner works in the store personally.
The owner of this cafe is famous for being kind.
I asked the owner about the business hours.
The owner decides the shop's days off.
The shop owners gathered and discussed prices.

examples.ko: 배달 앱에서는 점주가 메뉴를 직접 올려요.
examples.en: On a delivery app, the owner posts the menu directly.

explain: 편의점, 카페, 치킨집처럼 체인점의 주인을 가리킬 때 특히 많이 써요. 직접 부를 때는 '점주님'보다 '사장님'이 훨씬 자연스러워요. 본사와 계약해서 가게를 여는 사람은 '가맹점주'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used especially for the owners of chain stores like convenience stores, cafes, and chicken shops. When addressing someone directly, '사장님' is far more natural than '점주님'. An owner who contracts with headquarters is a '가맹점주'.

examples.en: The gardener is trimming the rose bushes.
My father worked as a gardener for a long time.

examples.ko: 우리 집 정원은 정원사가 관리해 줘요.
examples.en: A gardener looks after our house's garden.
Thanks to the gardener, the yard became tidy.
I want to become a gardener someday.

examples.ko: 공원 정원사는 아침마다 꽃에 물을 줘요.
examples.en: The park gardener waters the flowers every morning.

explain: '요리사', '미용사'처럼 '사'가 붙은 직업 이름이에요. 집에서 취미로 가꾸는 사람은 보통 '정원사'라고 하지 않고 '정원을 가꾸다'라고 말해요. 일로 하는 사람이라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Like '요리사' and '미용사', the '사' ending marks a profession. Someone who gardens at home as a hobby is not usually called a '정원사'; people say '정원을 가꾸다' instead. The word carries a sense of doing it as a job.

examples.en: Steel is made at a steel mill.
My father works at a steel mill on the southern coast.
The area near the steel mill is bright with lights even at night.
On a tour of the steel mill, I saw a blast furnace.
Thousands of people work at a large steel mill.

examples.ko: 제철소가 생긴 뒤로 이 도시가 커졌어요.
examples.en: This city grew after the steel mill was built.

explain: '제철'은 철을 만드는 일이고, 뒤에 '소'가 붙어 그 일을 하는 곳이 돼요. '제철 과일'의 '제철'은 그 계절에 한창인 때라서 전혀 다른 말이에요. 구리나 아연 같은 금속을 만드는 곳은 '제련소'라고 해요.
explain_en: '제철' is the making of iron, and '소' makes it the place. The '제철' in '제철 과일' is the season when something is at its best, a completely different word. A place that refines metals like copper or zinc is a '제련소'.

examples.en: There are many skyscrapers in Seoul.
From a high-rise apartment, you can see the whole city at a glance.
The wind blows hard around skyscrapers.

examples.ko: 새로 지은 초고층 호텔에서 하룻밤 잤어요.
examples.en: I stayed one night at a newly built high-rise hotel.
Riding a skyscraper elevator makes my ears feel blocked.

examples.ko: 초고층에 사는 친구가 있어서 가끔 놀러 가요.
examples.en: I have a friend who lives high up, so I visit sometimes.

explain: '초고층 아파트', '초고층 빌딩'처럼 건물 앞에 붙여서 써요. '고층'은 높은 층이고 '초고층'은 그보다 훨씬 높은 건물이에요. 뉴스나 부동산 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 같은 뜻의 '마천루'는 글에서 가끔 써요.
explain_en: It goes before building words: '초고층 아파트', '초고층 빌딩'. '고층' means high floors, while '초고층' is far taller. It is common in news and real estate talk; the synonym '마천루' appears occasionally in writing.

examples.en: He suffered a fatal injury in a traffic accident.
Thankfully, they say it is not a fatal wound.
It is not life-threatening, so a few days of rest is enough.

examples.ko: 이번 실수는 우리 회사에 치명상이 되었어요.
examples.en: This mistake was a fatal blow to our company.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 치명상을 입고도 끝까지 달렸어요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie kept running to the end despite a fatal wound.

examples.ko: 가슴에 입은 치명상 때문에 병원에 실려 갔어요.
examples.en: He was carried to the hospital because of a mortal wound in the chest.

explain: 보통 '치명상을 입다'로 써요. 목숨이 위험한 상처라서 가벼운 상처에는 쓰지 않아요. 가벼운 상처는 '경상', 심한 상처는 '중상'이라고 해요. 회사나 계획이 크게 망가질 때도 비유로 '치명상'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is usually '치명상을 입다'. Because it means a life-threatening wound, it is not used for minor ones: a light injury is '경상' and a serious one is '중상'. It is also used figuratively when a company or plan is badly damaged.

examples.en: On Parents' Day, I pinned a carnation on my parents.
Carnations are most often red.
On Teachers' Day, I gave my teacher a carnation.
I bought a bunch of carnations at the flower shop.

examples.ko: 카네이션 한 송이만 있어도 마음이 전해져요.
examples.en: Even a single carnation conveys your heart.
My mother showed off the carnation pinned on her chest.

explain: 한국에서는 5월 8일 어버이날과 5월 15일 스승의 날에 특히 많이 주고받아요. 부모님 가슴에 빨간 카네이션을 달아 드리는 풍습이 있어요. '카네이션을 달다', '카네이션을 드리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In Korea carnations are especially common on Parents' Day (May 8) and Teachers' Day (May 15). There is a custom of pinning a red carnation on a parent's chest. Use '카네이션을 달다' or '카네이션을 드리다'.

examples.en: Her nose bridge is high, so her profile is pretty.
My nose bridge is low, so my glasses keep sliding down.
Wrinkles form on the bridge of my nose when I laugh.
I pushed my glasses up the bridge of my nose.

examples.ko: 새 마스크가 콧대를 꽉 눌러서 아파요.
examples.en: The new mask presses hard on my nose bridge and it hurts.
I made my nose bridge look higher with makeup.

explain: 코의 위쪽 길게 이어진 선에 써요. 콧구멍이나 코끝은 다른 말이에요. 안경, 마스크, 화장 이야기에 자주 나와요. 비유로도 쓰는 말이라서 아래 표현을 같이 보세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 인기가 많아서 콧대가 높아요.
phrases.en: be stuck-up; look down on others
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘난 척하고 다른 사람을 얕보는 태도를 말해요. 반대로 '콧대를 꺾다'는 잘난 척하는 사람의 기를 눌러 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a proud attitude of looking down on others. '콧대를 꺾다' means to take a boastful person down a peg.
phrases.en_equiv: have one's nose in the air

explain_en: It refers to the long upper line of the nose; the nostrils and the tip are different words. It comes up in talk about glasses, masks, and makeup. It is also used figuratively, so see the expression below.

examples.en: The war created many evacuees.
The evacuees are staying in temporary shelters.
The school became a shelter for evacuees.
Volunteers handed out blankets to the evacuees.
Some evacuees lost their homes in the flood.

examples.ko: 피난민 아이들이 새 학교에 다니기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The evacuee children started attending a new school.

explain: 전쟁이나 재난의 위험을 피해 살던 곳을 떠난 사람에게 써요. 나라 밖으로 피한 사람은 '난민'을 더 많이 써요. 홍수나 지진으로 집을 잃은 사람은 '이재민'이라고도 해요. 한국전쟁 이야기에도 '피난민'이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to people who left home to escape the danger of war or disaster. For people who fled abroad, '난민' is used more. People who lost homes to floods or earthquakes are also called '이재민'. '피난민' often appears in stories about the Korean War.

examples.en: You have to bring writing tools to the exam room.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 필기구가 가득 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Writing tools are piled up on the desk.
I carry my writing tools in a separate part of my bag.
I bought new writing tools at the stationery store.
I had no pen, so I borrowed one from a friend.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 필기구가 종류별로 잘 정리되어 있어요.
examples.en: This shop has its writing supplies well organized by type.

explain: 펜, 연필처럼 글씨를 쓰는 도구를 한꺼번에 부를 때 써요. 말할 때는 '필기도구'를 더 많이 해요. 안내문이나 상품 분류에서 자주 봐요. 볼펜처럼 하나하나 말할 때는 이 말을 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is a group word for pens, pencils, and other writing tools. In speech, '필기도구' is more common. It shows up in notices and product categories. You would not use it for a single item like a ballpoint pen.

examples.en: The lower floors of this building have a parking lot.
If you go down to the lower level, you will find the subway station.

examples.ko: 하층에서 나는 공사 소리가 위층까지 올라와요.
examples.en: Construction noise from the lower floor travels up to the upper floors.

examples.ko: 하층 주민들은 홍수가 나면 피해가 커요.
examples.en: Residents of the lower floors suffer more when a flood hits.

examples.ko: 사회의 하층에서 일하는 사람들의 이야기를 다룬 책이에요.
examples.en: It is a book about people working in the lower layers of society.
We turned off the lights in order, starting from the lower floor.

explain: 건물의 층과 사회 계층 두 가지에 쓰는 글 투의 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 건물이면 '아래층'을 더 많이 써요. 반대말은 '상층'이에요. 사람을 하층이라고 부르면 낮추는 느낌이 있어서 조심해요.
explain_en: It covers both building levels and social classes, in a written style. In daily talk '아래층' is more common for buildings. The opposite is '상층'. Calling people '하층' sounds belittling, so be careful.

en: skate; thornback ray; fermented skate dish

examples.en: Fermented skate is famous as a strong-smelling food.
In Jeolla, people eat skate at feasts.

examples.ko: 처음 먹은 홍어는 코가 아플 정도로 독했어요.
examples.en: The first skate I ate was so strong it made my nose sting.
I bought a skate at the market.

examples.ko: 돼지고기, 묵은 김치와 같이 먹는 홍어삼합이 유명해요.
examples.en: Hongeo samhap, skate eaten with pork and aged kimchi, is famous.

examples.ko: 삭힌 홍어는 좋아하는 사람과 싫어하는 사람이 갈려요.
examples.en: Opinions on fermented skate split between lovers and haters.

explain: 삭혀서 먹는 요리로 유명해서 한국 사람들 사이에서도 좋아하는 사람과 싫어하는 사람이 확실히 갈려요. 홍어, 돼지고기, 묵은 김치를 함께 먹는 '홍어삼합'이 대표적이에요. 생선 이름이지만 음식 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is famous as a fermented dish, and even Koreans split sharply between lovers and haters. The classic way is '홍어삼합': skate with pork and aged kimchi. It is a fish name, but it comes up more in food talk.

en: venting anger; taking it out on someone

examples.en: Please do not take it out on others for no reason.
Some people vent their anger by cleaning.
That is not a conversation, it is just venting.
My friend sang loudly to blow off steam.

examples.ko: 어디에도 화풀이할 곳이 없어서 밖을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I had nowhere to vent my anger, so I walked outside.
If you need someone to vent to, tell me.

explain: 화가 난 마음을 터뜨리는 일인데, 화나게 한 사람이 아닌 다른 사람이나 물건에 풀 때 많이 써서 부정적이에요. '화풀이를 하다', '화풀이 상대'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '분풀이'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is the act of letting out anger, usually on someone or something other than the cause, so it sounds negative. Use '화풀이를 하다' and '화풀이 상대'. A similar word is '분풀이'.

en: take one's anger out on; vent anger

examples.en: Please do not take your anger out on me.
He took out his anger by throwing things.

examples.ko: 스트레스 받는다고 가족에게 화풀이하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take your stress out on your family.
Some of my friends vent their anger through exercise.
If I am upset, I will go to karaoke and blow off steam.
Why are you taking it out on me?

explain: '~에게/한테 화풀이하다'처럼 대상을 말해요. 그 사람이 화난 이유가 아닌데 터뜨린다는 느낌이에요. '화를 풀다'는 마음을 가라앉힌다는 좋은 뜻도 되지만, '화풀이하다'는 남에게 터뜨리는 나쁜 느낌이에요.
explain_en: The target takes '~에게/한테': '~에게 화풀이하다'. It implies the person is not the reason for the anger. '화를 풀다' can mean calming down in a good way, but '화풀이하다' is negative, letting it out on others.

examples.en: Our baby has started taking first steps.
The baby fell while practicing walking.

examples.ko: 걸음마가 빠른 아이도 있고 느린 아이도 있어요.
examples.en: Some children walk early and some walk late.

examples.ko: 할머니가 걸음마 하는 아기 손을 잡아 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma held the hand of the baby learning to walk.

examples.ko: 걸음마 신발은 가볍고 미끄럽지 않아야 해요.
examples.en: Shoes for toddlers should be light and non-slip.

examples.ko: 사진 속 아기는 아직 걸음마도 못 하는 때였어요.
examples.en: In the photo, the baby was at an age before even taking first steps.

explain: 아기가 처음 걷기 시작하는 것을 '걸음마를 시작하다', 걷는 데 익숙해진 것을 '걸음마를 떼다'라고 해요. '걸음마'는 걷는 동작 자체를 가리켜서 '걸음'과 달라요. 어른의 일에 쓰면 비유가 되는데 아래 표현을 보세요.

phrases.example: 우리 회사는 해외 시장에서는 아직 걸음마 단계예요.
phrases.en: in its infancy; just getting started
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 이제 막 시작해서 아직 많이 부족한 상태를 아기의 걸음마에 빗대요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compares a field that has only just started, and is still immature, to a baby's first steps.

explain_en: '걸음마를 시작하다' means a baby begins to walk, and '걸음마를 떼다' means the baby has got the hang of it. '걸음마' is the early walking itself, not just a step. For adults it becomes a metaphor; see below.

examples.en: I gave my father golf clubs for his birthday.

examples.ko: 골프채 한 세트는 값이 꽤 비싸요.
examples.en: A set of golf clubs is quite expensive.
I loaded the golf clubs, bag and all, into the car.
This golf club is light, so it is easy to use.
Holding a golf club for the first time felt awkward.
Each golf club has a different use.

explain: 운동마다 도구 이름이 달라서 야구는 '방망이', 테니스는 '라켓', 골프는 '골프채'라고 해요. 동사도 달라서 '골프를 치다', '골프채를 휘두르다'처럼 써요. 골프채 하나하나는 '드라이버', '아이언'처럼 이름이 따로 있어요.
explain_en: Each sport names its tool differently: '방망이' for baseball, '라켓' for tennis, '골프채' for golf. The verbs differ too: '골프를 치다' and '골프채를 휘두르다'. Individual clubs have their own names, like '드라이버' and '아이언'.

examples.ko: 그는 한국에 귀화해서 한국 이름을 지었어요.
examples.en: He became a Korean citizen and chose a Korean name.

examples.ko: 오 년 동안 살면 귀화할 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can I be naturalized after living here five years?
To be naturalized, you must take a Korean test.

examples.ko: 귀화한 뒤에도 고향 음식을 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: Even after naturalizing, I often cook food from my hometown.
My friend became a Canadian citizen last year.
The whole family gathered on the day of naturalization.

explain: '한국에 귀화하다'처럼 나라 이름에 '에'를 붙여요. '이민하다'는 다른 나라로 가서 사는 것이고, '귀화하다'는 그 나라 국적을 얻는 거예요. 이민을 갔다고 꼭 귀화한 건 아니에요. '귀화 시험', '귀화 신청'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: The country takes '에': '한국에 귀화하다'. '이민하다' means moving abroad to live, while '귀화하다' means getting that country's citizenship. Emigrating does not automatically mean naturalizing. It also appears in '귀화 시험' and '귀화 신청'.
